correctness.rationale: For every odd exponent k>=3 the power map is a unit-group permutation mod 2^n. Splitting input parities gives exact counts, and even-even scaling contributes exactly 2^(2k-2) lifts. Iterating the normalized recurrence gives a stable valuation formula for all nonzero targets, and Haar valuation masses give the necessary and sufficient q(k-2)<k moment bound. Cubic mean and variance follow from finite moment equations. Exhaustive independent finite counting checked 36 modulus/exponent pairs, 4088 residues, 1,398,096 input pairs and 180 further stabilization tests; infinite statements depend on the symbolic proof.

originality.rationale: The full accessible text of the primary 2023 diagonal-power-sum study concerns the cardinality of the image, not fiber-by-fiber counts or limiting density moments. The inspected 2003/2004 Broughan cube work likewise concerns existence of representations and modular obstructions. The exact finite dyadic multiplicity recurrence, valuation distribution, cubic variance 3/4 and integrability threshold are not implied by mere support-cardinality formulas. Related general local-zeta machinery presents a legitimate residual coverage risk.
residual_risks: General p-adic local-zeta/pushforward-density literature could contain a dominating representation-density theorem not found in inspected references.
A separately published or unindexed modular two-power multiplicity table could overlap with the recursion.
Some unindexed mathematical literature may contain equivalent dyadic fiber-density formulas; this possibility is not ruled out.

value.rationale: The originating publication studies which residue classes are sums of powers; for every odd exponent all dyadic classes are representable, making support size blind to their sharply unequal multiplicity. An exact full-fiber law for all odd exponents is a natural quantitative invariant. The exact critical moment k/(k-2), finite cubic variance 3/4, and infinite fifth-and-higher variance provide a structural boundary tied to the singular scaling near zero, with potential use in local distribution and congruence comparison.
